description:
On a sheltered brick wall.  They seem to be old remains, and are quite hardy: almost a year later, they still look the same.  Broken open one of these -- inside were some shed larval skins, what looked like an intact larva, what might have been egg impressions at the bottom, and a bunch of frass. Have a photo, if it will help. 

So does the surrounding matrix constitute both food and protection supplied by the female when she lays the eggs? Otherwise, what would they be eating, here on a brick wall? 

Don't know if the larval mass is related to the egg array.  There were two of the former; one was near the egg array and one was a foot or so away.
